concept_name: The four angles add up to 360°

item.question: Three angles of a quadrilateral are 75°, 95° and 110°. Find the fourth angle.
steps: A diagonal splits the quadrilateral into two triangles, so its angles add up to 180 + 180 = 360.
The three known angles add up to 75 + 95 + 110 = 280.
The fourth angle is 360 − 280 = 80.
item.text:
Worked example: Three angles of a quadrilateral are 75°, 95° and 110°. Find the fourth angle.
1. A diagonal splits the quadrilateral into two triangles, so its angles add up to 180 + 180 = 360.
2. The three known angles add up to 75 + 95 + 110 = 280.
3. The fourth angle is 360 − 280 = 80.
Answer: 80°

item.question: In parallelogram ABCD, ∠A = 30°. Find ∠B, ∠C and ∠D.
steps_tex: $AB \parallel CD$ with transversal $AD$, so $\angle A + \angle D = 180$.
$AD \parallel BC$ with transversal $AB$, so $\angle A + \angle B = 180$, and $\angle B = 150$.
$\angle C + \angle D = 180$, so $\angle C = 180 - 150 = 30$.
steps: AB || CD with transversal AD, so ∠A + ∠D = 180.
AD || BC with transversal AB, so ∠A + ∠B = 180, and ∠B = 150.

item.question: In parallelogram ABCD, AB = 4 cm and AD = 5 cm. Find CB and CD, and say why ∆ABD ≅ ∆CBD is wrong.
steps_tex: Join the diagonal $BD$.
$\angle BAD = \angle DCB$, because they are opposite angles of the parallelogram.
$AD \parallel BC$ with transversal $BD$, so $\angle ADB = \angle CBD$ (alternate angles).
$BD$ is common, so by $AAS$, $\triangle ABD \cong \triangle CDB$.
So $CB = AD = 5\text{ cm}$ and $CD = AB = 4\text{ cm}$.
$\triangle CBD$ would match $C$ with $A$ but $B$ with $B$, claiming $AB$ equals $CB$, yet $AB$ is $4\text{ cm}$ and $CB$ is $5\text{ cm}$.
item.answer_tex: $CB = 5\text{ cm}$ and $CD = 4\text{ cm}$; $\triangle ABD \cong \triangle CBD$ is wrong because its vertices do not match
steps: Join the diagonal BD.
∠BAD = ∠DCB, because they are opposite angles of the parallelogram.
AD || BC with transversal BD, so ∠ADB = ∠CBD (alternate angles).
BD is common, so by AAS ∆ABD ≅ ∆CDB.
So CB = AD = 5 cm and CD = AB = 4 cm.
∆CBD would match A with C but B with B, claiming AB equals CB, yet AB is 4 cm and CB is 5 cm.
item.answer: CB = 5 cm and CD = 4 cm; ∆ABD ≅ ∆CBD is wrong because its vertices do not match

concept_name: The diagonals of a parallelogram bisect each other

item.question: In parallelogram EASY the diagonals AY and ES meet at O, with AY = 10 cm and ES = 6 cm. Find OA, OY, OE and OS, and say why ∆AOE ≅ ∆SOY is wrong.
steps: AE = YS, because they are opposite sides of the parallelogram.
AE || YS, so ∠OAE = ∠OYS and ∠OEA = ∠OSY (alternate angles).
By ASA, ∆AOE ≅ ∆YOS, so OA = OY and OE = OS.
OA = OY = 10 ÷ 2 = 5 cm and OE = OS = 6 ÷ 2 = 3 cm.
∆SOY would pair A with S and E with Y, but A matches Y and E matches S.
item.answer: OA = OY = 5 cm and OE = OS = 3 cm; ∆SOY is in the wrong order
item.text:
Worked example: In parallelogram EASY the diagonals AY and ES meet at O, with AY = 10 cm and ES = 6 cm. Find OA, OY, OE and OS, and say why ∆AOE ≅ ∆SOY is wrong.
1. AE = YS, because they are opposite sides of the parallelogram.
2. AE || YS, so ∠OAE = ∠OYS and ∠OEA = ∠OSY (alternate angles).
3. By ASA, ∆AOE ≅ ∆YOS, so OA = OY and OE = OS.
4. OA = OY = 10 ÷ 2 = 5 cm and OE = OS = 6 ÷ 2 = 3 cm.
5. ∆SOY would pair A with S and E with Y, but A matches Y and E matches S.
Answer: OA = OY = 5 cm and OE = OS = 3 cm; ∆SOY is in the wrong order

concept_name: The diagonals of a rhombus meet at right angles

item.question: In rhombus GAME the diagonals meet at O, with GM = 8 cm and EA = 6 cm. Find the angle at O, GO and EO.
steps: A rhombus is a parallelogram, so its diagonals bisect each other: GO = MO and EO = AO.
In ∆GEO and ∆MEO: GE = ME, GO = MO, and EO is common, so ∆GEO ≅ ∆MEO by SSS.
So ∠GOE = ∠MOE, and together they make 180, so each is 90.
GO = 8 ÷ 2 = 4 cm and EO = 6 ÷ 2 = 3 cm.
item.answer: The diagonals meet at 90°; GO = 4 cm and EO = 3 cm
item.text:
Worked example: In rhombus GAME the diagonals meet at O, with GM = 8 cm and EA = 6 cm. Find the angle at O, GO and EO.
1. A rhombus is a parallelogram, so its diagonals bisect each other: GO = MO and EO = AO.
2. In ∆GEO and ∆MEO: GE = ME, GO = MO, and EO is common, so ∆GEO ≅ ∆MEO by SSS.
3. So ∠GOE = ∠MOE, and together they make 180, so each is 90.
4. GO = 8 ÷ 2 = 4 cm and EO = 6 ÷ 2 = 3 cm.
Answer: The diagonals meet at 90°; GO = 4 cm and EO = 3 cm

steps: Diagonal BD makes four equal angles a: two at B and two at D.
In ∆ADB, a + a + 50 = 180, so the two angles a add up to 180 − 50 = 130.

item.text:

steps_tex: (i): Adjacent angles add up to $180$, so $\angle E = \angle R = 180 - 40 = 140$, and $\angle A = \angle P = 40$.
(ii) $\angle Q = \angle S = 180 - 110 = 70$, and $\angle R = \angle P = 110$.
(iii): The diagonal $XV$ bisects $\angle V$ and $\angle X$, so $\angle V = 30 + 30 = 60$ and $\angle X = 60$.
Then $\angle U = \angle W = 180 - 60 = 120$.
(iv): The diagonal $OE$ bisects $\angle E$ and $\angle O$, so $\angle E = 20 + 20 = 40$ and $\angle O = 40$.
Then $\angle A = \angle I = 180 - 40 = 140$.
item.answer_tex: (i) $\angle E = 140^\circ$, $\angle A = 40^\circ$, $\angle R = 140^\circ$; (ii) $\angle Q = 70^\circ$, $\angle R = 110^\circ$, $\angle S = 70^\circ$; (iii) $\angle V = \angle X = 60^\circ$, $\angle U = \angle W = 120^\circ$; (iv) $\angle E = \angle O = 40^\circ$, $\angle A = \angle I = 140^\circ$
steps: (i) Adjacent angles add up to 180, so ∠E = ∠R = 180 − 40 = 140, and ∠A = ∠P = 40.
(iii) The diagonal XV bisects ∠V and ∠X, so ∠V = 30 + 30 = 60 and ∠X = 60.
(iv) The diagonal OE bisects ∠E and ∠O, so ∠E = 20 + 20 = 40 and ∠O = 40.
item.text:
$1$. (i): Adjacent angles add up to $180$, so $\angle E = \angle R = 180 - 40 = 140$, and $\angle A = \angle P = 40$.
$2$. (ii) $\angle Q = \angle S = 180 - 110 = 70$, and $\angle R = \angle P = 110$.
$3$. (iii): The diagonal $XV$ bisects $\angle V$ and $\angle X$, so $\angle V = 30 + 30 = 60$ and $\angle X = 60$.
$4$. Then $\angle U = \angle W = 180 - 60 = 120$.
$5$. (iv): The diagonal $OE$ bisects $\angle E$ and $\angle O$, so $\angle E = 20 + 20 = 40$ and $\angle O = 40$.
$6$. Then $\angle A = \angle I = 180 - 40 = 140$.
Answer: (i) $\angle E = 140^\circ$, $\angle A = 40^\circ$, $\angle R = 140^\circ$; (ii) $\angle Q = 70^\circ$, $\angle R = 110^\circ$, $\angle S = 70^\circ$; (iii) $\angle V = \angle X = 60^\circ$, $\angle U = \angle W = 120^\circ$; (iv) $\angle E = \angle O = 40^\circ$, $\angle A = \angle I = 140^\circ$
